It has no gimmick.
Five years on the list.
slides.subline: Soko, Hannam-dong — No. 89 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026, and ranked every year since 2022

slides.label:
Straight years Soko has appeared on
Asia's 50 Best Bars — 2022 to 2026

slides.title:
The East-West part
is not in the glass.
slides.body:
Most of Seoul's ranked bars are built on a concept you can describe in a sentence — a hanok courtyard, a zero-waste programme, a storybook. Soko does not have one. Le Monde Diplomatique Korea reports it opened in 2017 in a Hannam-dong alley, styled after a reception room from Korea's early-20th-century opening years, in wood and velvet.

What it has instead is a method. Owner-bartender Son Suk-ho is a World Class competitor and a former head bartender at Coffee Bar K, and Korean coverage credits him with Japanese-school precision. The Korea Herald singles out the dry martini alongside Mr. Peanut, a build of whisky, amaro cordial and peanut.

So the meeting of East and West that the 50 Best write-up describes is not an ingredient list. It is Japanese bar technique, poured in a Korean room dressed as the era when Western drinking first arrived here.

Taste is always personal.

caption:
A basement door in Hannam-dong, and no concept to explain.

Soko sits at No. 89 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 — its fifth straight year ranked. Open since 2017 under bartender Son Suk-ho, it trades themes for technique: a dry martini, and Mr. Peanut in whisky, amaro cordial and peanut.

Research, not a visit. Hours and prices as of September 2026, and taste is personal.

Sources in the last slide. Save it for Seoul.
